review_kind: independent adjudication of a contested critical finding (worker-19 F-1 / HF-06)

hard_failures.finding: The quantifier expansion of the class conclusion uses WHOLE-CURVE single-q containment ('gamma subset J^-(q) intersect M', D5 witness gamma([0,T))), while the same file's canonical visibility predicate is TAIL-based ('exists q in I+ AND t0 in [0,T) such that gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q)', :220). Whole-curve containment implies tail containment but not conversely, so quantifiers.formal is strictly weaker than the conclusion it expands: a development in which some q sees a tail but no q sees the whole curve satisfies the formal clause and fails the class conclusion. quantifiers.negation (:84-88) uses 'is visible from I+' (tail semantics), so it does not negate quantifiers.formal. The schema's own visibility.definition at :220 states that requiring the whole geodesic to lie in J^-(q) 'would misclassify a geodesic that starts in the exterior and ends inside the black-hole region' - the file self-refutes the wording used in its formal block. The rev9 note (:17-19) declares the tail predicate canonical but the formal expansion and D5 were not updated (editing residue, not a notation dispute).
hard_failures.falsifier: a line in the pinned bytes where quantifiers.formal or D5 constrains a tail gamma([t0,T)); or a causality/monotonicity lemma showing whole-curve non-containment follows from tail non-containment; or a demonstrated reading in which 'gamma subset J^-(q)' denotes a tail. See report.falsifier for the full list.
hard_failures.impact: G-FORM must not close on this revision; the F1 verdict(s) accepting these bytes did not test the expansion against visibility.definition.

D5 defines the witness as gamma([0,T)) contained in J^-(q): whole parameter range.
visibility.negation_conclusion negates the tail predicate over every q and every t0.
quantifiers.negation uses 'visible from I+' (tail) and is not the literal negation of quantifiers.formal.
ordered expansion has forall gamma -> not_exists q only; no t0 binder.
self-refutation: the file states the whole-curve reading misclassifies the intended scenario.
conclusion.statement_formal references the predicate by name, so the defect is confined to the expansion and D5; the repair is local and semantics-preserving.
strictness argument and separating scenario stated; causal pasts are past-closed, not future-closed, so earlier parts of gamma need not lie in J^-(q).

D0 is a mixed-type domain while the binder is a pair (s,delta); 'or the smooth-with-decay default' supplies no pair and 'the class is fixed at these values' conflicts with forall over D0. Confirms worker-19 F-2 as written; severity adjudication deferred.
